title: Incline-Bench Cable Pullover
summary: A lat isolation done lying on an incline bench, pulling a cable from behind your head down to your hips, so the lats are loaded hard at full stretch.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: cable station with an adjustable pulley; adjustable (incline) bench.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.3 for triceps (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly triceps total.
Library rating 0.2 for chest: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 0.2 for upper back: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly upper back total.

setup.text: Set an incline bench with its head end facing a low cable, and take a rope or straight bar with your arms overhead.
Lie back with a slight elbow bend and let the cable pull your arms back until your lats are stretched.
Sweep the handle down in an arc to your hips, driving with your elbows.
Return slowly to the full stretch.

form_cues.cue: Pull the bar over to your hips
Return to a deep lat stretch
Keep the elbow angle fixed. If your elbows bend and straighten, it turns into a triceps press.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows into a triceps extension.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds no ramp-up sets; make the first working set a touch lighter if you like.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 10-15 reps, stopping about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less isolation, Less stable, Less constant tension.
